items.title: Rethinking the Value of Agent-Generated Tests for LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents
items.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) code agents increasingly resolve repository-level issues by iteratively editing code, invoking tools, and validating candidate patches. In these workflows, agents often write tests on the fly, but the value of this behavior remains unclear. This raises a central question: how does agent-written testing relate to task outcomes and resource use during repository-level issue resolution? To better understand the role of agent-written tests, we analyze 5,000 recorded agent runs produced by six strong LLMs on SWE-bench Verified using the lightweight mini-SWE-agent scaffold. Our results show that test writing is common for most models. GPT-5.2 is an exception: it rarely writes new test files while achieving a resolution rate close to the top-ranked model. Test-writing frequency varies widely across models. Within a given model, it differs less between resolved and unresolved tasks. When tests are written, their files contain substantially more statements that print runtime values than assertions that check conditions. We then compare baseline prompts with revised prompts that encourage or discourage writing new test files for four models. Agents start or stop writing test files as requested on 36.8%-93.2% of tasks. Resolved-task totals differ by 0-13 out of 500 per model, with no statistically significant difference, while API calls or token use differ substantially for three models. Similar resolution totals can therefore hide substantial differences in how agents test and how many resources they use.

items.title: LLM-as-Code: Agentic Programming for Agent Harness
items.summary: Every major LLM agent framework gives the LLM the role of orchestrator; the model decides what to do next, when to call tools, and when to stop. We argue that token explosion, control-flow hallucination, and unreliable completion are not implementation bugs but architectural consequences of assigning the deterministic work of looping, branching, and sequencing to a probabilistic system. A better prompt or a stronger model cannot guarantee the reliability of the LLM agent. We therefore propose Agentic Programming, in which the program governs all control flow, and the LLM is itself part of it, an adaptive component we call LLM-as-Code and invoke only where a task calls for reasoning or generation. Within each call the model keeps full flexibility, but it cannot alter the program's execution path. With control in the program, the LLM's context is built from the execution history's call tree and forms a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Each call's context length is then determined by its call depth rather than by accumulation over steps. A case study of computer-use agents shows that the design is practical, not just a theoretical stance, substantially improving the stability of long visual operation sequences.Code is available at https://github.com/FuzzyKuji/OpenProgram.

items.title: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks
items.summary: We study the fingerprinting of agentic cyberattacks. Our objective is to reliably infer information about the attacker's configuration, such as LLM version and harness, from telemetry. To achieve this, we introduce a technique we call shibboleth traps: modular honeypot services designed to elicit discriminative behaviors from agentic attackers. The traps make informative interactions a condition for obtaining resources the agent seeks, eliciting model declarations and characteristic writing without requiring a successful prompt injection. To achieve harness fingerprinting, we introduce general mechanisms to indirectly probe peculiar execution behaviors of harnesses. These probes reveal how a harness masks secrets in tool output, enforces command time limits, and schedules tool calls, using only the effects visible in subsequent requests. We show that combined declarative and behavioral inference distinguishes among 15 candidate models with an average 90% top-1 accuracy, with behavioral classifiers evaluated on held-out harnesses or task families. In a separate experiment across four harnesses, fixed probe rules identify the correct harness with 92% accuracy. When instructed to conceal their identity, agents still leave useful behavioral evidence even as their declarations become uninformative.

items.title: EvoAgent: An Evolvable Agent Framework with Skill Learning and Multi-Agent Delegation
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, but skills are usually written by hand, and letting an agent change them on its own calls for explicit user control. We report on EvoAgent, an evolvable agent framework built for a foreign trade assistant, and share the engineering choices behind it. We organize the agent as a harness of four components (reasoning, context engineering, tools and state) and confine self-improvement to the user's persistent state: profile, memory and skills. Skills are multi-file packages with lazily loaded references, matched in three stages (keyword, embedding, LLM). The main agent can delegate to sub-agents with their own context, and long histories are compressed while an index of recoverable resources is kept. An offline loop reviews completed sessions to update the profile and memory and to propose skills; in the open-source release a skill changes only after the user confirms the proposal. On 172 foreign trade test cases scored by an LLM judge on five dimensions, GPT-5.2 with EvoAgent scored about 28% higher than GPT-5.2 called directly with only the final query. This is a single run judged by the model under test, so it measures the harness as a whole rather than any one mechanism, and swapping in GPT-4.1 or Qwen3.5-35B-A3B lowered the scores relative to calling those models directly. Several mechanisms described here were added after the version we evaluated and are not evaluated. The evaluation data is proprietary, so the results are for reference only. An open-source release of the code, which is not the evaluated business version, is available at https://github.com/Focus-AI-Center/Mentarc-EvoAgent

items.title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents
items.summary: External tool calls are a major running cost of an LLM agent, while its training objectives align almost exclusively with task completion. In a step-level diagnosis of Qwen3.5 trajectories at two model sizes on GAIA, a long-horizon tool-use benchmark, we find that most contain removable calls, at a similar rate at both sizes. Some methods add an efficiency reward to the objective to reduce the call count, but introduce problems of their own: the anchor they price calls against is computed from the policy's own rollouts (e.g., the group's shortest correct rollout) and so moves with the policy; training can drift toward a collapsed policy that issues no tool call at all, a degeneracy seen in published reports and in our 27B baseline; and a training run delivers a single operating point, so the user cannot trade efficiency against capability. We present CARE-PO (Controllable Anchored Relative Efficiency Policy Optimization) to mitigate these problems. The efficiency reward prices calls against a reference budget anchored to the task's own difficulty and fixed before training. Injecting a successful trajectory from the training data into each online GRPO rollout group and charging for evidence a trajectory never gathers ease the drift toward a collapsed call count. Shaping the cost curve by an effort tag in the prompt yields an efficiency and a capability operating point from a single training run. On GAIA, five of the six operating points across three model sizes improve on their base model in success rate and call count at once. On four held-out multi-hop benchmarks the result is size-dependent: at 27B and 4B success rate is held or raised at a lower call count, while at 9B both operating points trade success rate for fewer calls. The call count remains well above zero throughout training at all three sizes.

items.summary: Nghiên cứu tác động của việc viết test bởi LLM agents trong quy trình sửa lỗi mã nguồn, so sánh hiệu suất và tài nguyên sử dụng.
items.title: Rethinking the Value of Agent-Generated Tests for LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents

items.authors: Junjia Qi, Zichuan Fu, Jingtong Gao, Wenlin Zhang, Hanyu Yan, Xian Wu, Xiangyu Zhao
items.summary: Đề xuất mô hình Agentic Programming, nơi chương trình điều khiển luồng và LLM chỉ thực hiện reasoning/generation.
items.title: LLM-as-Code: Agentic Programming for Agent Harness

items.authors: Dario Pasquini, Reworr, Giuseppe Ateniese, Manish Bhatt, Sergej Epp
items.summary: Phát triển kỹ thuật shibboleth traps để nhận diện LLM và harness trong các cuộc tấn công agentic.
items.title: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks

items.authors: Aimin Zhang, Jiajing Guo, Fuwei Jia, Chen Lv, Boyu Wang, Fangzheng Li
items.summary: Giới thiệu EvoAgent, framework cho phép agent tự học kỹ năng và phân công công việc cho sub-agents.
items.title: EvoAgent: An Evolvable Agent Framework with Skill Learning and Multi-Agent Delegation

items.authors: Xiaoyang Ye, Xiao Yao, Hairui Zhu, Yiying Yang, Bei Gan, Jinliang Lu, Tengjin Weng, Yuan Yao, Wenhao Jiang
items.summary: Đề xuất CARE-PO để điều chỉnh số lượng tool calls của LLM agents, cải thiện hiệu suất và giảm chi phí.
items.title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents

result.markdown:
- Nghiên cứu tác động của việc viết test bởi LLM agents trong quy trình sửa lỗi mã nguồn, so sánh hiệu suất và tài nguyên sử dụng. - [arxiv.org](http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07900v3)
- Đề xuất mô hình Agentic Programming, nơi chương trình điều khiển luồng và LLM chỉ thực hiện reasoning/generation. - [arxiv.org](http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15874v3)
- Phát triển kỹ thuật shibboleth traps để nhận diện LLM và harness trong các cuộc tấn công agentic. - [arxiv.org](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12386v1)
- Giới thiệu EvoAgent, framework cho phép agent tự học kỹ năng và phân công công việc cho sub-agents. - [arxiv.org](http://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20133v5)
- Đề xuất CARE-PO để điều chỉnh số lượng tool calls của LLM agents, cải thiện hiệu suất và giảm chi phí. - [arxiv.org](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12125v1)
